verdict.root_cause: Cart's requests intermittently stall because its Valkey-backed cart store is slow: in the degraded traces every Valkey command cart issues — HGET, HMSET and EXPIRE alike — pays a near-identical ~300ms penalty executed sequentially, pushing AddItem to ~0.9s, while cart's own handler self-time stays sub-millisecond and no span is error-marked [tr_8a5ff61ece01]. Cart itself is healthy and serving: it logs normal info-level cart-store operations through the end of the window with no exceptions, timeouts or connection failures [tr_89136cac2840], and no deploy, config edit or flag change is recorded for cart or flagd in the queried window [tr_94c45a3eb2f0, tr_8a5acf363c50]. The mechanism is waiting on a slow datastore dependency; the alert fan-out to checkout, frontend, frontend-proxy and load-generator a minute later is inherited latency.
verdict.reasoning: The only positive signal on the board is the trace decomposition: all excess duration sits in self-time of cart's Valkey client spans, uniform across read, write and TTL commands, while flagd resolution and all peer services stay at low-millisecond latency [tr_8a5ff61ece01]. That localises the wait to cart's store and excludes cart's own CPU/GC/locks, errors and retries, and upstream peers. Cart being alive and writing ordinary logs with no connection or 'no space' text [tr_89136cac2840] rules out process_freeze, network_partition, datastore_corruption and disk_fill. Empty change logs [tr_94c45a3eb2f0, tr_79115c58b092, tr_8a5acf363c50] remove in-window deploy/config/flag triggers, though those queries start at onset and leave the pre-onset hours unobserved. The cart span-metrics series is absent across both incident and baseline windows [tr_db2cca187d6f], so it is a broken monitor and evidence of nothing either way. Fix is to clear the stalled store path rather than revert an artifact.
open_questions: The Valkey/cart-store instance was never examined directly — its logs, memory pressure, eviction and fsync/persistence behaviour could distinguish blocking I/O from a saturated server, and that changes the fix.
The trace sample covers ~01:40–01:48 and is truncated, and the cart log dropped its middle section, so the minutes around 02:09:16 were never directly observed [tr_8a5ff61ece01, tr_89136cac2840].
All change queries began at onset and looked forward, so a deploy, config edit or latency-injecting flag landing shortly before 02:09:16 remains unqueried [tr_94c45a3eb2f0, tr_8a5acf363c50].

alternatives.root_cause: A pre-onset feature flag or config value injecting artificial delay into cart's Valkey call path, applied just before 02:09:16 and therefore outside every change query's window.
alternatives.why_not: Purely inferential — no change record was ever retrieved for the pre-onset interval, and the uniform per-command cost is equally explained by a store-side stall that needs no change at all.

alternatives.root_cause: The Valkey cart store is itself resource-exhausted (memory pressure forcing eviction/swap, or connection-pool saturation), making every command queue ~300ms.
alternatives.why_not: No metric or log from the Valkey instance was collected to show any resource at its ceiling; from cart's side this is indistinguishable from generic store slowness, so the broader latency class is the safer claim.

proposal.expected_effect: No action is proposed, so no change in any signal should be observed. The investigation should instead continue: pull the Valkey/cart-store instance's own logs, memory/eviction and persistence (fsync/BGSAVE) behaviour, and re-run the change queries over the hours *before* 02:09:16, which no current result covers.
proposal.if_wrong: This abstention is wrong if someone produces evidence that the ~300ms uniform penalty originates inside cart's own process — e.g. cart-side connection-pool exhaustion, a stuck client multiplexer, or a client-side timer — rather than in the Valkey server. Concretely: if cart's Valkey client spans show queue/wait time before command dispatch, or if the store answers other clients at sub-millisecond latency while only cart is slow, then restart_service on cart becomes defensible and should be proposed. It is also wrong if a pre-onset deploy or flag change for cart/flagd turns up in a backward-looking change query, which would make rollback_image or revert_config the correct class.
proposal.risk: Not acting leaves AddItem at ~0.9s and the inherited latency at checkout, frontend, frontend-proxy and load-generator unmitigated for as long as the Valkey degradation persists; if the store is filling or thrashing, the condition can worsen into errors. That cost is accepted here because the alternatives are worse: restart_service on cart does not touch the component the traces blame, would drop cart's warm in-process state and open connections, and on a saturated or blocking-I/O store the reconnect storm can deepen the stall; rollback_image and revert_config both have an unmet precondition — no deploy, config edit or flag change is recorded for cart or flagd in any queried window [tr_94c45a3eb2f0, tr_8a5acf363c50], and no prior image tag or configuration is on record to restore to.
proposal.blast_radius: None from this proposal, since nothing is executed. For reference, the service that would have been touched is cart, whose inbound callers in this incident are checkout and frontend (and transitively frontend-proxy and load-generator); any later action on cart will be visible to all four as reset connections during container recreate. The actions that would actually address the mechanism — restore_store (FLUSHALL on the cart store) and reconnect_service — are both listed UNAVAILABLE in this brief, so the correct fix is outside what this system may do today.

triage_judgement.reasoning: Cart alerted first and the checkout/frontend/proxy tier followed a minute later, which looks like a real fault propagating upward rather than a single isolated warning. Cart's dependency (flagd) and the shared downstreams are worth probing, though the fault class is only a weak prior.
